support: I laughed out loud the first evening I saw it myself: a chimney that has burned nothing for eleven years, drawing a cloud of smoke down into itself.
Until they go, every clear evening the old chimney smokes in reverse over the schoolyard, and I stand at the gate grinning up at it.
WV12-P04.5.note: The writer laughs out loud at, and grins up at, the comic sight of a long-cold chimney seeming to smoke in reverse; neither statement reads as ironic, and the writer never praises, mourns, criticizes or worries about the chimney, so admiration (the closest rival) is not stated.
